text:
Both summaries are accurate. Each correctly reports the opening-hours proposal, Ross's objection, that no agreement was reached, that hours stay unchanged, and that Helen will bring a revised proposal in November. Both also get the reading-program dates, the volunteer deadline, the roof replacement recommendation and the next meeting date right. Neither has a factual error. A's "send two launch-day volunteers" is slightly loose, since managers send names, but it isn't misleading.

The real difference is fitness for the brief. Response A runs to roughly 190 words, well over the 120-word limit. Much of that is filler, such as "Thank you for taking the time to review…", "so please plan accordingly" and "during this period," which a busy manager doesn't need.

Response B is about 120 words, essentially at the limit. It keeps every key point and adds the visitor figures (11 vs 64), which explain why the proposal was made. It also flags the volunteer request clearly as an action.

On accuracy the two are even. On coverage B is slightly better. On concision and meeting the word limit, B is clearly better.

Verdict: B
